clue.text: Joy living with one's pet ghosts ?

parts.note: a pet is an animal kept at home
ghosts are spirits of the dead

explanation.surface: A lonely person finds happiness living with the ghost of a beloved pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living with' is a link joining the pet and the ghosts side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: High spirits or exuberant cheerfulness are called animal spirits, a natural sense of vigour and gladness.

clue.text: His is Pope's "proper study"

parts.note: Alexander Pope wrote that the proper study of mankind is man, which is the field of a scientist of humanity

explanation.walkthrough: Pope's 'Essay on Man' says 'The proper study of mankind is man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of human societies and cultures makes humankind the subject of research.

clue.text: As one put-up account has it, his father nearly killed him

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the words before it read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A story recounts how a man's father almost killed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put-up' turns AS I into ISA; 'has it' is a link. In Genesis Abraham nearly sacrificed his son.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Abraham was about to sacrifice his son on a mountain until an angel stopped him.

clue.text: Environment the Earth and poems strangely share

indicators.note: strangely suggests these letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Earth and poetry share a common environment, a reflective thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges EARTH and POEMS; 'the', 'and' and 'share' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The air or mood surrounding a place, its surroundings.

clue.text: Colonist pays his way

explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer who sets up home in a new land; and one who settles up a bill, paying what is owed.

clue.text: Ramp caused by a stroke of the pen, say ?

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds the same as the phrase

parts.note: a pen stroke makes an ink line

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a slope could come from a single pen stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or gradient, a surface tilted upwards.

clue.text: Part of the US radio wave transmission

indicators.note: transmission means carrying across, so the phrase carries the answer within it

explanation.surface: A radio wave transmission broadcasts across part of America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern state of America.

clue.text: "Every man over forty is a —" (G. B. Shaw)

definitions.text: "Every man over forty is a —" (G. B. Shaw)

parts.words: "Every man over forty is a —" (G. B. Shaw)
parts.note: Bernard Shaw wrote this in 'Maxims for Revolutionists', calling every middle-aged man a rogue

explanation.walkthrough: A completion clue: fill the blank in Shaw's maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or villain, a dishonest rascal, as Shaw called men past forty.

clue.text: Martin's zero rating changed by metempsychosis

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Martin's, with the possessive s kept as a letter
zero is the figure 0, read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A man named Martin has his zero-rating altered, by some mystic process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges MARTINS, O and RATING; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Metempsychosis is the passing of a soul into a new body after death.

clue.text: Wounding-with it a cut arm perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the words before it might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A cut arm is a wounding injury, the clue seems to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the nine letters of IT A CUT ARM; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wounding causes trauma, injury to body or mind.

clue.text: Lovesick, frog

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme frog who would a-wooing go is a lovesick suitor courting Miss Mouse

explanation.walkthrough: The old nursery song 'A frog he would a-wooing go' tells of a frog going courting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovesick suitor courting someone is one who woos.

clue.text: Sways firm foundations

explanation.definitionFit: Sways back and forth, as a cradle moves; and solid stone bedrock that a building stands on.

clue.text: This paper's about-face

indicators.note: about in about-face turns the word face back to front

parts.note: a clock face is its dial

explanation.surface: A newspaper makes a sudden U-turn in its editorial line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about-face' is read as 'about' turning the word for 'face' backwards; ''s' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid paper is a writing paper with a ribbed texture from the wires of the mould.

clue.text: Put the girl out of the ring presently

indicators.note: out of here means outside, so the girl's name goes round the ring

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl is ordered out of the boxing ring for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; 'out of' sets ANN outside O.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or shortly.

clue.text: Formal gold ring ? How original !

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal
or is gold in heraldry
to ring someone is to dial them

explanation.surface: Admiring a formal gold ring, someone exclaims at its originality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is a link. 'ring' looks like jewellery but is a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing from the very beginning, first and earliest.

clue.text: The ball is not in his court, he takes it

definitions.text: The ball is not in his court, he takes it

parts.words: The ball is not in his court, he takes it
parts.note: in tennis doubles, a player who reaches across to hit a ball meant for a partner's side is said to poach it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the idiom 'the ball is in your court'; in doubles tennis one who steals a partner's shot is a poacher, as a hunter takes game from another's land.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a player who intercepts a shot belonging to a partner's half of the court is called this.

clue.text: In a manner consistent with electrical flex ?

parts.note: AC is alternating current, electricity
flex is electrical cording

explanation.surface: Someone asks what conforms with the rules on electrical cables.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a flex is the insulated cord on an electrical appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing with or following a source, as in 'as stated by'.

clue.text: Listener gets involved in a murder

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the words after it are mixed

explanation.surface: A witness who overheard something finds themselves mixed up in a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A MURDER; 'gets' and 'in' are links. 'Listener' sounds like a person but is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound is what does the hearing.

clue.text: Swiss lake plant

explanation.definitionFit: A lake in central Switzerland named after its city; and alfalfa, a clover-like fodder crop.

clue.text: Bound to finish without trimming

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: an end is a finish
lace is a trimming on clothes

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is bound to finish the work without adding any trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means 'outside', not 'lacking'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied or entwined, as if laced together.

clue.text: Convict after : sentence ? Some delay here

indicators.note: after places the convict's word behind the sentence's word

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
an old lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict awaits sentence and wonders about the delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a link. LAG is British slang for a habitual prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval between cause and effect is a pause or wait.

clue.text: The rope-walk ?

parts.note: a rope-walk is a long shed for making rope, but here it is a riverside path where horses pulled barges by rope

explanation.walkthrough: A rope-walk is really a ropemaker's shed; here it is the path along a canal where horses hauled barges.
explanation.definitionFit: A path beside a canal or river used by horses hauling boats.

clue.text: To travel by railway's just bloody

parts.note: to go is to travel
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Travelling by train is a bloody nuisance, someone complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link; 'bloody' looks like British swearing but is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in or marked by spilt blood, as a violent scene is.

clue.text: Defect in feminine rule?

parts.note: F is the grammar abbreviation for feminine
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rule made by women has a flaw in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish or imperfection, a weakness in something.

clue.text: It's madder to chafe at a single article

parts.note: to chafe is to rub
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Rubbing at one item makes it all the more maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madder' reads as 'more mad' but is the dye plant; 'It's', 'to' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubia is the botanical genus of the madder plant, source of a red dye.

clue.text: Orwell, grave poet

explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell's real surname was Blair; and Robert Blair wrote the poem 'The Grave'.

clue.text: She doesn't sound an entirely upright girl.

definitions.text: She doesn't sound an entirely upright girl.

parts.words: She doesn't sound an entirely upright girl.
parts.note: said aloud the girl's name sounds like a person who leans, one not quite standing straight

explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name sounds like 'leaner', one who leans and so is not entirely upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, short for Helena or Magdalena.

clue.text: Entry into the field of fashion, say?

indicators.note: say here means spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: style is fashion

explanation.surface: Breaking into the fashion business is a kind of entry into a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' suggests a profession; it is a farmer's field, entered by steps over a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of steps letting walkers climb over a fence or wall into a pasture.

clue.text: Vicar, hair ruffled, causes an uproar

indicators.note: ruffled hair is messed up, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A vicar with tousled hair causes a commotion in the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' rearranges VICAR and HAIR; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy mock serenade or din, a cacophony of pans and shouting.

clue.text: Scott told tales for one of them

definitions.text: Scott told tales for one of them

parts.words: Scott told tales for one of them
parts.note: Walter Scott wrote 'Tales of a Grandfather' for his young grandson

explanation.walkthrough: Scott's 'Tales of a Grandfather' was a history of Scotland written for his grandson.
explanation.definitionFit: Children of one's sons or daughters, for whom a grandparent might tell stories.
